URL: https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/23/uk-climate-crisis-national-security-report-suppressed-starmer-ed-miliband
The Guardian — published Wed 23 September 2026 22:21 BST (2026-09-23T21:21:33Z); updated Thu 24 Sep 06:19 BST — Fiona Harvey

HEADLINE: UK shares findings of damning climate crisis national security report suppressed under Starmer
STANDFIRST: El Niño poses critical threat to nations' defences, says Ed Miliband in presentation to global foreign ministers

FACTS:
- The UK has warned countries around the world that the climate and nature crises and the coming El Niño threaten their national security and defence, presenting foreign ministries with the findings of a report suppressed under Keir Starmer.
- Ed Miliband, the UK's foreign secretary, made the presentation to the foreign ministers of the EU as well as Kenya and other countries on Wednesday night (23 Sep) at a private meeting during the UN General Assembly in New York — the first such discussion among foreign ministers.
- The presentation was based on the joint intelligence committee (JIC) report by the UK's spy chiefs, which found the collapse of natural systems around the world would lead to conflict, migration and food shortages.
- The JIC report was scheduled to be published last October but was suppressed on the eve of its launch by Downing Street. A redacted version was issued in January under the Freedom of Information Act; ministers have continued to resist calls for the full report to be made public.
- Miliband acted with the backing of Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
- Miliband will appoint a new special representative for climate security, plus a new ministerial taskforce on "the national security and resilience risks of a changing climate and nature loss", with military and security experts as well as climate scientists.
- He announced £330m for the Global Environment Facility, the main international fund for protecting nature, to go towards protecting forests, oceans and other critical ecosystems in developing countries.
- The closed-door meeting followed Miliband's public speech on Monday 21 Sep at the UN General Assembly on climate and national security (text on gov.uk: "What climate security means now" — Foreign Secretary at New York Climate Week).

QUOTE — ED MILIBAND, Foreign Secretary: "We face an El Niño that is already set to be the most intense in living memory. This will intensify climate shocks that compound and cascade across borders, threatening food and water security, displacing communities, putting pressure on markets and scarring economies."

QUOTE — ED MILIBAND: "Climate change and nature loss have never been issues for climate and environment ministers alone. They are defining challenges for our citizens, our economies, our foreign policy and our national security."

QUOTE — ED MILIBAND (Wednesday night): "The countries fit for the future will be those that see climate and nature as intrinsic to economic and national security. Countries that anticipate risks and invest in resilience before crises hit. Countries that seize the incredible opportunities the clean energy transition presents. Countries that don't just see the connections but act on them." He added: "That is why the UK is placing climate and nature security at the heart of our national security and foreign policy decision-making."

QUOTE — RICHARD NUGEE, retired general and security expert: "If a bridge is washed away, it has the same impact whether it's done by [a foreign power] or the climate. The climate crisis will affect food security, energy security, water security, and lead to migration and potentially the recruitment of farmers to [terrorist organisations such as] Isis. Countries should absolutely be treating this as a national security issue."

QUOTE — ADRIAN RAMSAY, Green Party MP for Waveney Valley: "It's good that the foreign secretary is presenting the findings of this crucial report to ministers from other governments. But it begs the question, why are MPs in this country still being denied access to the full report? And, most importantly, why has our government still not published its response to how it will address the stark findings?"

Related Guardian data (same day): "Huge El Niño projected to cause more than 450,000 deaths by February" — forecast additional heat-related deaths Sep 2026–Feb 2027 vs 1996–2025: Nigeria 31,320; Indonesia 19,251; Sudan 17,430; India 15,670; Brazil 13,271. Projected increase in acute food insecurity due to El Niño by region: Asia and the Pacific +8.2m (on 73.3m); East Africa +5.9m (52.9m); Western and central Africa +6m (48.9m); South America and the Caribbean +12.2m (28.7m); Southern Africa +12.2m (16.3m); Central America +4.2m (5m). Source: WFP regional scenario analyses of 45 countries.
